To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
innate immune receptors recognize microbial symbionts to mediate beneficial cross-talk between hosts and microbes.
innate immune receptors sense microbial symbionts to promote colonization and host development, and that this function is evolutionarily conserved in both invertebrates and vertebrates.
innate immune recognition of the gut microbiota promotes development and homeostasis of host tissues and the immune system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis for the recognition of the microbiome by the host immune system and the consequences of this recognition for host health and disease.
the mechanisms that underlie host-microbial symbioses.
the molecular and cellular interactions between the immune system and the microbiota that are essential for host health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
innate immune receptors have evolved to promote symbiotic interactions with the microbiota, and that the immune system is a critical regulator of host-microbial symbiotic relationships.
PRRs are required for the establishment of symbiotic relationships between hosts and their microbiota.
the innate immune system is required to maintain a mutualistic relationship between the host and the microbiota, and that PRRs play a central role in this process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune system has evolved to recognize the microbiota as a beneficial partner.
the microbiota signals through pattern-recognition receptors to promote host development and immunity.
the host immune system has evolved to recognize and respond to the resident microbiota to promote mutualism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system has evolved to recognize the microbiota as an essential part of the host and to promote symbiotic relationships.
the immune system is a key regulator of the microbiota.
the innate immune system evolved to recognize the microbiota and to promote host-microbial symbioses.
